claims.claim: Publisher implements the closed outcome classification, exact lineage/currentness checks, and ordinary fast-forward/already-included paths; operational receipts are not publication success.
Recovery plans bind current main and original reviewed blob identities. Deterministic source materialization preserves unrelated main content and checks ancestry, overlap, scope and currentness.

Recovery uses ordinary RUN and Runtime completion/result surfaces, distinguishes pre-admission failures, and retains prior PASS as provenance. The missing transport resolver binding is corrected using the existing reviewed resolver.

Runtime recovery verification records evidence validity and reused-versus-executed provenance, checks proof context and raw integrity, and routes invalid or unknown proof through bounded existing verification.
Semantic review scope identifies the recovered candidate and marks prior PASS as provenance only; publication requires the recovered candidate's exact canonical review decision.
The publication workflow routes exact decision events and replay through the durable continuation, admission, result resume, fresh-review and Publisher paths with identity checks and CAS ownership.

Currentness, competing-source, admission, integration and evidence guards remain present alongside focused counterexample fixtures for stale bindings, duplicate admission, lost wake, missing proof and changed proof context.
The publication-specific normative leaf is linked from README, Project Contract and self-host navigation and documents section-scoped retention, redirects and historical authority.
Local real-Git and synthetic fixtures cover RUN-326 planning divergence, material overlap, ordinary publication, recovery, currentness and proof reuse without external credentials.
Existing publication and correction validators remain in use. The repair changes only one operator import, preserving the prior candidate and its separation from later TASK-326 operations.
